requirements.evidence: Contract is implemented exactly: `app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:25` matches the required invokable signature; `app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-14` defines the three string-backed cases; `app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7` extends RuntimeException and `InactiveQueueException` is reused at `app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:35`. Queue filtering and ordering are at `app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:89-98`, fairness at `:42-46` and `:104-115`, the inactive-queue DB read under the queue lock at `:29-36`, exactly-once candidate locking and skipping at `:68-79`, and the returned model is marked at `:52-57`. Both required docs are updated: `docs/business-rules.md` adds the implementation bullets ('**Full ordering:** `priority` desc, then `issued_at` asc, then `id` asc') and `docs/architecture.md` rewrites the 'Call the next ticket' flow ('Lock the queue row; reject if inactive (read from the DB)').

conventions.evidence: Uses the project's Action pattern (`app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:14-25`), ships a Pest feature test (`tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:1-303`), and keeps docs/CHANGELOG in sync (`docs/business-rules.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`). One deviation: the call transition is re-implemented at `app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:52-55` instead of reusing the existing `Ticket::call()` primitive (conventions.md 'already here -> reuse').

security.evidence: No user input or rendered output is added. The action sets only the three mutable fields directly (`app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:52-55`), avoiding mass assignment, and the docblock explicitly leaves authorization to the caller as the task requires (`:22-23`); no Livewire, Blade, upload, or secret surface is touched.

tests.evidence: `tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php` covers ordering and tie-breaks (`:38-118`), all three modes plus the no-eligible-ticket exceptions (`:120-154`), inactive/stale-queue rejection (`:164-175`), the fairness streak, its reset, the no-normal fallback and mode-ignoring (`:177-276`), write-once fields (`:57-68`), and a simulated concurrent `Ticket::call()` skip (`:277-303`).

simplicity.evidence: Lean structure: one action, two small private helpers (`app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:64-116`), and a constant for the streak limit (`:16-17`); no service/repository layer or speculative abstraction. The three-line call transition at `:52-55` duplicates `Ticket::call()` (see the conventions issue), which is the only avoidable duplication.

readability.evidence: Clear names (`claim`, `nextCandidate`, `priorityStreakIsFull`), short methods, and docblocks/comments that explain the non-obvious snapshot/race handling (`app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:19-24`, `:75-77`, `:84-86`); the tests read as behavior descriptions (`tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:38-58`).

scope.evidence: Only task-related files are touched: the action, enum and exception, the two docs the task names (`docs/business-rules.md`, `docs/architecture.md`), the CHANGELOG entry required by the project conventions, and the new test file. No unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: The action re-implements the call transition (`status`, `called_at`, `called_by_user_id` + `save()`) instead of reusing `Ticket::call()`, duplicating the existing write path and bypassing any invariants that primitive enforces; if the entity-membership check in `Ticket::call()` is the reason it was avoided (authorization is out of scope here), document that in the docblock.

The concurrent test injects the competing `Ticket::call()` from a `DB::listen` callback on the same connection/transaction, so it exercises the skip/re-check branch but not real row-lock contention; a two-connection test (or a comment noting the limitation) would better prove the exactly-once claim.

Two generic global helper functions are declared in the feature test file; in Pest these can collide with helpers in other feature files and are usually placed in `tests/Pest.php` or as file-local closures.

review.summary: The change adds the `CallNextTicket` domain action, the `CallMode` enum and `NoWaitingTicketsException`, implementing queue-scoped candidate selection, deterministic priority/age/id ordering, the 3-priority fairness rule, inactive-queue rejection, and exactly-once locking, with updated docs and a broad Pest suite. Requirements, security and tests are strong; the main cleanup is reusing `Ticket::call()` for the marking transition instead of duplicating it, plus minor test nits, so the pull request would be approved after those small changes.
